name: Papain
short: Case reports: life-threatening anaphylaxis and asthma, mostly after breathing in papain at work. Review in cancer patients of enzymes incl. papain, mainly by mouth: side effects mainly gut upsets.
text: Most of the safety evidence on papain concerns allergy after workplace exposure, mainly by breathing in the powder, although one report notes that both occupational and non-occupational papain allergies have been documented. A case report describes occupational sensitivity to papain with life-threatening anaphylaxis, including hives, angioedema (swelling) and throat symptoms, which disappeared once he moved away from direct exposure. Other case reports describe asthma in the supervisor of a meat-tenderiser factory after long-term contact with papain dust; asthma, rhinitis and conjunctivitis in a 50-year-old herbs and spices packer, confirmed by challenge testing; and IgE-mediated papain allergy in a 53-year-old sausage-plant worker who also had mouth itching and tongue and throat swelling after eating kiwi fruit and figs; that report reviewed 13 published patients with papain allergy, 11 of whom had been sensitised through the respiratory tract. Two further reports, available only as titles, describe papain-induced allergic reactions and occupational allergy to papain. An observational study of 11 patients with latex allergy who had all had anaphylaxis caused by papaya, a fruit whose most allergenic proteins include papain, concluded that sensitivity to papaya increases the risk of anaphylaxis, and therefore of death, in people with latex allergy; this concerns the fruit, not papain products. The only oral evidence cited is a systematic review of the proteolytic enzymes bromelain, papain and chymotrypsin in cancer care, which included 15 studies with 3,008 patients with cancer, in which the enzymes were mainly taken by mouth alongside conventional treatment; it found enzyme therapy was well tolerated in most cases, with side effects mainly gastrointestinal, such as diarrhoea or bloating; the abstract does not say how many of the products contained papain. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
